content: The dosage of Penicillin V potassium should be determined based on the sensitivity of the causative microorganisms and the severity of the infection. It should also be adjusted according to the patient’s clinical response. For adults and children aged 12 years and older, the following dosage recommendations apply: 1. Streptococcal infections (mild to moderately severe) of the upper respiratory tract, including scarlet fever and erysipelas: Administer 125 to 250 mg (200,000 to 400,000 units) every 6 to 8 hours for a duration of 10 days. 2. Pneumococcal infections (mild to moderately severe) of the respiratory tract, including otitis media: Administer 250 to 500 mg (400,000 to 800,000 units) every 6 hours. Continue treatment until the patient has been afebrile for at least 2 days. 3. Staphylococcal infections (mild infections of the skin and soft tissue): Administer 250 to 500 mg (400,000 to 800,000 units) every 6 to 8 hours. It is essential to perform culture and sensitivity tests to confirm the appropriateness of treatment. 4. Fusospirochetosis (Vincent’s infection) of the oropharynx (mild to moderately severe infections): Administer 250 to 500 mg (400,000 to 800,000 units) every 6 to 8 hours. 5. Prevention of recurrence following rheumatic fever and/or chorea: Administer 125 to 250 mg (200,000 to 400,000 units) twice daily on a continuous basis. 6. Prophylaxis against bacterial endocarditis in patients with congenital heart disease or rheumatic/acquired valvular heart disease undergoing dental or surgical procedures of the upper respiratory tract: Administer 2 grams of Penicillin V (1 gram for children under 60 lbs) 1 hour before the procedure. Follow this with 1 gram (500 mg for children under 60 lbs) 6 hours after the initial dose.
